title: Obtain whole-law spatial mixing from bounded semigroup variance
statement: Put S0=|x0|1,V=1+sum(lambda+lambda^-1),D0=4V(1+S0)^2,A0=4(n+V)(1+S0)^2. Conditional Poisson tails give P_pi(|N|>s)<=min(1,exp(D0-s)); fixed-degree weighted tails<=C_L exp(D0-B/2),C_L=16(4L+4)^(L+1), while pi(x0)>=exp(-A0), including rare actual classes. For targeteta set R0=1+3G0 h Q0 C_L,B=ceil[4(D0+A0+R0+eta^-1+10)],T=ceil[a(B)(A0+eta^-1+10)]. Then b(B) and exp(-2T/a(B))<=eta^2 exp(-A0)/64. Nonexplosion follows from finite invariant mean intensity and the accepted embedded-chain holding-time argument. For bounded0<=f<=1, stationary nonreversible variance dissipation and osc(Pt f)<=1 imply Var_pi(Pt f)<=exp(-2t/a(B))Var_pi(f)+b(B). Initial-atom domination gives |P_T f(x0)-pi f|<eta uniformly overALLsuchf, hence ENTIRE law TV. All majorants/cutoffs/time use finite rational fixed-power arithmetic; exp(-A0) is never output as an exponentially huge binary denominator. No uniform full spatial L2 gap is assumed or concluded.
